text:
Will Borgen has become the Bruins' feel-good signing. The Boston Globe called the steady defenseman the perfect addition, and Boston.com called him a game-changer on the defense corps, both on Nov. 10. He's playing about 19 minutes a night, throwing hits (49) and blocking shots (29), with 2 goals and 5 points in 21 games.

Our numbers are warmer on the results than the process. Boston has 52% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on at five on five, a bit below the team without him, and he's been outshot in those minutes. The results have been much better than that: our on-ice luck measure has him around 15 goals ahead of his chances, the kind of cushion that rarely lasts a full season.

None of that makes him a poor signing. Evolving-Hockey had him slightly above the middle of NHL defensemen last season in New York, mostly on even-strength defense. It does mean the praise was written during a stretch of good fortune, and Boston has since lost three straight. How he holds up without it is the next chapter.
